nodes.name: ▶ Run Manually
nodes.notes: Use this to kick off a run by hand (testing, ad-hoc batches, etc.).

nodes.name: ⏰ Schedule (every 10 min)
nodes.notes: Runs automatically every 10 minutes. Each execution picks up the next 1,000 pending users. Disable the Manual Trigger when going live.

nodes.name: 📋 Read Config Sheet
nodes.notes: Reads the Config sheet. Expected columns: 'setting' and 'value'. Rows: guild_id, role_id, bot_token.

nodes.name: ⚙️ Extract Config
nodes.notes: Pulls guild_id, role_id, and bot_token out of the Config sheet rows into a single clean item.

nodes.name: 👥 Get Pending Users
nodes.notes: Reads only rows where 'status' is blank (not yet processed). Returns row numbers so we can update the exact row. If 0 rows are returned, the workflow ends naturally here — no more work to do.

nodes.name: 🔁 Loop (1 user at a time)
nodes.notes: Processes one user per iteration so each row in the sheet is updated immediately after its Discord call. Output 0 = current user, Output 1 = all users done (workflow ends).

nodes.name: 🎭 Assign Discord Role
nodes.notes: Makes the Discord PUT /roles API call. Handles 204 success, 404 not-in-server, 429 rate limit, and generic errors. Always returns user_id + row_number + status so the next node can update the sheet regardless of outcome.

nodes.name: ✅ Update Row Status
nodes.notes: Updates the exact sheet row (by row_number) with: status (done/failed/not_in_server/rate_limited), timestamp, and any error message. If this workflow ever crashes, only rows still showing blank status will be retried next run.

parameters.content:
## 🚀 Discord Mass Role Assignment

### What this workflow does
1. **Reads config** (Guild ID, Role ID, Bot Token) from the *Config* sheet
2. **Fetches all pending users** from the *Users* sheet (rows where `status` is blank)
3. **Assigns the role** to each user via Discord's REST API
4. **Stamps each row** with `done`, `failed`, `not_in_server`, or `rate_limited` + a timestamp
5. **Loops** — on the next run, only rows still showing blank `status` are picked up, giving you automatic crash-resume

### Google Sheets setup
**Config sheet** (tab name: `Config`)
| setting | value |
|---------|-------|
| guild_id | 123456789012345678 |
| role_id | 987654321098765432 |
| bot_token | Bot MTIz... |

**Users sheet** (tab name: `Users`)
| user_id | status | timestamp | error |
|---------|--------|-----------|-------|
| 123456789012345678 | | | |
| 234567890123456789 | | | |

> Leave `status` blank for pending rows. Rows already marked `done` are automatically skipped.

### Before first run
- Replace `YOUR_SPREADSHEET_ID` on the three Google Sheets nodes
- Connect your Google Sheets credential
- Set the `bot_token` cell in the Config sheet (include the `Bot ` prefix)
- Make sure your bot has `MANAGE_ROLES` permission and sits **above** the target role in the server hierarchy

### Throughput & timing
- ~4 assignments/second (250 ms gap between successful calls)
- 10,000 users ≈ 42 minutes per run
- 600,000 users ≈ 600 × 10-min scheduled runs ≈ 4 days at full pace
- To go faster: run multiple instances with disjoint user lists in separate sheets

### Status values written to the sheet
| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `done` | Role assigned successfully ✅ |
| `not_in_server` | User has left the server — skip forever |
| `rate_limited` | Hit Discord rate limit — will retry next run |
| `failed` | API error — see `error` column for details |
